_comment: Home ports on the new company screen, colored on the globe by how good a start they are. Ranked (2026-10-08, after commodity prices were halved) by an estimate of each port as an HQ: the best loop of 2 or 3 ports from it for a Scooter 20 (the only ship at level 1), a Laker (level 2) and a Feeder 100 (level 5), each in $ a minute (cargo margin x sale bonuses, less tolls, fuel and repairs, over sailing, docking, lock and convoy time), scored 8 x Scooter + 4 x Laker + 2 x Feeder; a port where a Scooter can't make money isn't offered. excellent: the top 5 in 5 different market regions (Conakry, Dublin, Shanghai, Cabo San Lucas, Rome), shown in bright shining green. great: the next 20 (green). fair: the 20 after (yellow). hard: 20 well-known ports where a Scooter still clears a profit, but a thin one (red). great_lakes: every Great Lakes port (blue), offered with a warning: the locks shut every winter and from the second year the lake ports freeze in (an icebreaker, from $8M, keeps them open). Notes give each port's best Scooter run. Every other port can't be picked. Recheck after changing markets.json, ship models or ports.

great_lakes.note: a real challenge, far harder than any coast. Every winter (with seasonal closures) the Seaway, Welland Canal and Soo Locks shut, Dec 31 to late March, cutting the lakes off from the sea; from year 2 the lake ports freeze in too, mid-January to late February, unless you station an icebreaker: from $8M (level 8).
